practices.title: A Shared Study Space
practices.instructions: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals to form a word that fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0). Write your answers in CAPITAL LETTERS.
practices.passage:
Careful (0) {{0}} was needed when students at Greenfield School proposed turning an unused classroom into a shared study space. The teachers had received complaints about noisy (17) {{17}} in the library, where pupils were trying to work during lunch.

items.explanation: BEHAVE → BEHAVIOUR (noun). 'complaints about noisy behaviour' requires a noun after the adjective 'noisy'. Context: “The teachers had received complaints about noisy behaviour in the library, where pupils were trying to work during lunch.” Common trap: behave (verb) and behavioural (adjective) cannot fill the noun position.

CHOOSE → CHOICE (noun). 'given a choice between A and B' is a fixed pattern. Context: “At the first meeting, students were given a choice between creating a completely silent room and providing an area for group projects.” Common trap: choose is a verb; chosen is a participle.

CONCLUDE → CONCLUSION (noun). 'reach the conclusion that ...' expresses the group's final judgement. Context: “After listening to both sides, the committee reached the conclusion that a flexible room would be more useful.” Common trap: conclude is a verb, not a noun.

CONSTRUCT → CONSTRUCTIVE (adjective). 'constructive criticism' means useful feedback intended to improve a plan. Context: “A teacher offered constructive criticism of the original design, pointing out that the movable tables might block the entrance.” Common trap: construction refers to building and is a noun.

CREATE → CREATIVITY (noun). 'show considerable creativity' needs an abstract noun for original ideas. Context: “Rather than abandon their idea, the students showed considerable creativity by designing two separate zones.” Common trap: creative is an adjective.

DECIDE → DECISION (noun). 'make the final decision' requires a singular count noun. Context: “The head teacher made the final decision once the safety plan had been approved.” Common trap: decide is a verb; decisions is plural.

DEVELOP → DEVELOPMENT (noun). 'during the development of the project' names a process. Context: “During the development of the project, volunteers discovered that younger and older pupils had different working habits.” Common trap: develop is a verb.

DIFFERENT → DIFFERENCES (noun). 'reflected those differences' needs a plural count noun referring to the contrasted habits. Context: “The completed room reflected those differences without favouring either group.” Common trap: different is an adjective.

practices.title: Reopening the Riverside Trail

items.explanation: EXCITE → EXCITEMENT (noun). 'caused genuine excitement' needs a noun for enthusiasm. Context: “The proposed (0) {{0}} of a riverside walking trail caused genuine excitement among local families.” Common trap: exciting is an adjective describing the event.

EXIST → EXISTING (adjective). 'the existing route' describes a path already there. Context: “The path had been closed for years, but the council hoped to make use of the existing route instead of cutting through untouched woodland.” Common trap: existence is a noun.

EXPECT → UNEXPECTED (adjective). 'an unexpected problem' expresses a problem not anticipated. Context: “During their first inspection, volunteers found an unexpected problem: part of the wooden bridge had been damaged by flooding.” Common trap: expected reverses the intended meaning.

EXPLAIN → EXPLANATION (noun). 'a clear explanation of why...' needs a singular count noun. Context: “An engineer gave a clear explanation of why the bridge needed repairs before anyone could cross it safely.” Common trap: explain is a verb.

HIGH → HEIGHT (noun). 'measure the height of the railings' uses the measurement noun. Context: “She also measured the height of the railings, as children would be using the trail.” Common trap: high is an adjective.

INTEND → INTENTION (noun). 'its intention was to reopen' states an aim or purpose. Context: “The council stated that its intention was to reopen the path without disturbing wildlife along the river.” Common trap: intentional is an adjective.

LOCATE → LOCATION (noun). 'a safer location for a platform' specifies a place. Context: “After considering several alternatives, the team selected a safer location for a small observation platform.” Common trap: located is a participle.

LONG → LENGTH (noun). 'the length of the route' names a distance measurement. Context: “The length of the route was slightly reduced so walkers would avoid a protected nesting area.” Common trap: long is an adjective; lengthy implies excessive duration.

EXCITE → EXCITING (adjective). 'an exciting programme' says the broadcast will interest listeners. Context: “The students therefore planned an exciting programme that would include music, interviews and reports about school clubs.” Common trap: excited describes a person's feeling.

EXIST → EXISTENCE (noun). 'the existence of an old room' states that the room was there. Context: “Few pupils had known about the existence of an old recording room beside the library.” Common trap: existing is an adjective.

EXPECT → EXPECTATIONS (noun). 'set realistic expectations' is a plural noun for what they hoped to achieve. Context: “After cleaning it, the volunteers set realistic expectations for their first broadcast.” Common trap: unexpected is an adjective.

EXPLAIN → EXPLANATION (noun). 'provided an honest explanation' requires a noun after the adjective. Context: “When listeners complained about background noise, the team provided an honest explanation and promised to improve the sound quality.” Common trap: explain is a verb.

HIGH → HIGHER (adjective). 'a higher number ... than the first' uses a comparative adjective. Context: “A later episode attracted a higher number of listeners than the first.” Common trap: height is a noun.

INTEND → INTENTION (noun). 'their original intention had simply been to share' describes the intended aim. Context: “The students' original intention had simply been to share useful information, but their station soon became a place where quieter pupils could make their voices heard.” Common trap: intentional is an adjective.
